name: Kyoto
summary: Golden and silver pavilions, thousands of red torii at Fushimi Inari, the Arashiyama bamboo grove, Gion's lantern-lit lanes and Nishiki Market's food stalls.

months.note: Cold and dry; quiet after the New Year shrine visits in the first days of January.
Coldest stretch with occasional snow on temples; plum blossoms start late in the month.
Warming up; cherry blossoms usually begin in the last week of March and crowds build.
Peak cherry blossom in early April, one of the busiest times of the year; Golden Week starts on 29 April.
Golden Week crowds in early May, then pleasant and green; Aoi Matsuri on 15 May.
Rainy season (tsuyu) brings humid, wet days and lighter crowds.
Hot and humid; the Gion Matsuri festival runs all month and packs central Kyoto.
Hottest month; Obon and the Gozan Okuribi bonfires (16 Aug) draw domestic crowds.
Still hot, with typhoon season peaking; Silver Week holidays can be busy.
Comfortable autumn weather; Jidai Matsuri on 22 October.
Autumn leaves peak from mid-November into early December, Kyoto's other busiest season.
Late autumn colour early in the month, then cold; many places close or get busy around New Year.

tips.title: Visa-free for short stays
tips.body: Travellers from visa-exempt countries such as the US can stay up to 90 days for tourism without a visa. You need a passport valid for your whole stay and usually proof of onward travel.

tips.title: Use Visit Japan Web for faster arrival
tips.body: Visit Japan Web creates QR codes for immigration and customs that you can scan at automated kiosks on arrival. It is optional in 2026, and paper cards are still accepted. Set up your account about two weeks before you fly.

tips.title: JESTA is not needed yet
tips.body: Japan passed a law on 29 May 2026 to create JESTA, an electronic travel authorization for visa-exempt visitors, but it will not launch before 2028. Ignore websites that charge for 'early JESTA registration'.

tips.title: Departure tax tripled to ¥3,000
tips.body: Since 1 July 2026 the International Tourist Tax on leaving Japan is ¥3,000, up from ¥1,000. In most cases it is already included in your airfare.

tips.title: Kyoto's higher hotel tax (from March 2026)
tips.body: Since 1 March 2026 Kyoto charges an accommodation tax per person per night based on the room rate: ¥200 under ¥6,000; ¥400 for ¥6,000–19,999; ¥1,000 for ¥20,000–49,999; ¥4,000 for ¥50,000–99,999; and ¥10,000 at ¥100,000 or more. The room rate counts service charges but excludes meals and consumption tax.

tips.title: Tax-free shopping is now a refund at the airport
tips.body: From 1 November 2026, visitors pay the full price including tax in shops and get the consumption tax back after customs checks the goods at departure. You must spend at least ¥5,000 per shop per day, and you need your passport plus all items and receipts. Leave time at the airport, because purchases with a missing item or receipt are not refunded.

tips.title: Carry some cash
tips.body: Japan still relies heavily on cash, so check whether a place takes cards before you order. You can withdraw yen at most ATMs, at airports or at banks.

tips.title: Don't tip
tips.body: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can cause embarrassment or confusion. The price you see is what you pay.

tips.title: Get an ICOCA card or mobile ICOCA
tips.body: ICOCA works on JR lines, private railways, buses and some taxis in Kansai. It also works at convenience stores and vending machines. It is available in Apple Pay and as Mobile ICOCA on Android, and you can top it up at station machines or convenience stores.

tips.title: How Kyoto buses work
tips.body: On Kyoto buses you pay when you get off, and drivers only give change for ¥1,000 notes. IC cards work on most buses but not on Yasaka bus lines. Big suitcases are unwelcome, so send luggage ahead with a delivery service.

tips.title: Gion's private alleys: no photos
tips.body: Residents have banned photography in Gion's privately owned alleys and streets, with signs warning of a ¥10,000 fine. Reports say the fine is not legally binding. Don't photograph geiko or maiko without asking first.

tips.title: Check your medicines before you pack
tips.body: Without a permit (Yakkan Shoshomei) you can bring up to one month's supply of prescription medicine and two months' of other medicines for personal use. Over-the-counter products with pseudoephedrine (such as Sudafed and Vicks inhalers) or codeine are banned, and stimulants are prohibited. Narcotics and psychotropics need advance permission, so carry your prescription and a doctor's letter.

tips.title: Plugs and voltage
tips.body: Japan uses two flat parallel-prong plugs at 100 V AC. Bring an adapter, and check that your devices accept 100 V.

tips.title: Emergency numbers
tips.body: Dial 110 for police and 119 for fire or ambulance.

places.name: Kinkaku-ji
places.blurb: Zen temple whose gold-leaf pavilion sits over a mirror pond.

places.name: Ginkaku-ji
places.blurb: Zen temple with the Silver Pavilion, a raked-sand garden and a hillside moss walk.
places.tip: Entry went up to 1,000 yen on 1 April 2026.

places.name: Kiyomizu-dera
places.blurb: Hillside temple famed for its wooden stage over the valley and the Otowa spring.

places.name: Nijo Castle
places.blurb: Tokugawa shogun's castle, known for Ninomaru Palace's nightingale floors and its gardens.

places.name: Kyoto Imperial Palace
places.blurb: Former imperial residence set in the large Kyoto Gyoen park.

places.name: Tea Ceremony Camellia FLOWER
places.blurb: Small English-language tea ceremony house in a machiya near Ninenzaka.

places.name: Nishiki Market
places.blurb: Narrow covered food street of about 100+ stalls, nicknamed 'Kyoto's Kitchen'.

places.name: Gion
places.blurb: Historic geisha district of teahouses and wooden machiya along Hanamikoji and Shirakawa.
places.tip: No photos in the private side lanes off Hanamikoji: fines are posted.

places.name: Gion Corner
places.blurb: Theatre staging short showcases of maiko dance and traditional arts.

places.name: Yasaka Pagoda
places.blurb: Five-storey pagoda that forms Higashiyama's classic sloping-street view.

places.name: Kyoto International Manga Museum
places.blurb: Manga library and museum in a former elementary school.

places.name: Kyoto Station Building
places.blurb: Hiroshi Hara's 1997 station complex with shops, a rooftop skyway and long escalators.

places.name: Maruyama Park
places.blurb: Public park behind Yasaka Shrine, known for its lit weeping cherry.

places.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
places.blurb: Head Inari shrine with thousands of vermilion torii climbing Mt Inari.
places.tip: Open 24 hours. Go early or late to beat the crowds.

places.name: Arashiyama Monkey Park Iwatayama
places.blurb: Hilltop park with free-roaming macaques and city views, reached by a steep 20–30 min climb.

places.name: Kurama-dera
places.blurb: Mountain temple above Kurama village, linked by a forest trail to Kibune.

places.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
places.blurb: Path through towering bamboo beside Tenryu-ji and Nonomiya Shrine.

places.name: Higashi Hongan-ji
places.blurb: Jodo Shinshu head temple with one of the world's largest wooden halls, near Kyoto Station.

places.name: Yasaka Shrine
places.blurb: Gion's guardian shrine and home of the Gion Matsuri, lit with lanterns at night.

places.name: Ninenzaka & Sannenzaka
places.blurb: Preserved stone-stepped lanes of shops and teahouses leading to Kiyomizu-dera.

places.name: Philosopher's Path
places.blurb: Two-kilometre canal-side stone path between Ginkaku-ji and Nanzen-ji, lined with cherry trees.

places.name: Eikan-do
places.blurb: Temple famed for its autumn maple colours and night illuminations.

places.name: Heian Jingu
places.blurb: 1895 shrine with a giant torii and a paid strolling garden.

places.name: Yasaka Koshindo
places.blurb: Tiny temple hung with colourful kukuri-zaru charms.

places.name: Kodai-ji
places.blurb: Zen temple founded by Hideyoshi's widow, with gardens and a bamboo grove.

places.name: Hachidaime Gihey
places.blurb: Rice-focused restaurant run by a rice merchant, serving donabe-cooked set meals.

places.name: Kamo River
places.blurb: River through central Kyoto with walking banks and summer dining terraces.

places.name: Pontocho
places.blurb: Lantern-lit alley of restaurants and bars along the Kamo River.

places.name: Gion Kappa
places.blurb: Late-night izakaya serving kushiyaki skewers.

places.name: Tenryu-ji
places.blurb: Head Rinzai Zen temple with Muso Soseki's 14th-century Sogenchi pond garden.

places.name: Unagi Hirokawa
places.blurb: Popular grilled-eel restaurant near the bamboo grove.

places.name: Togetsukyo Bridge
places.blurb: Wooden-railed bridge over the Katsura River against Arashiyama's hills.

places.name: Keifuku Randen tram
places.blurb: One-car streetcar linking Arashiyama with Ninna-ji and Ryoan-ji.

places.name: Ninna-ji
places.blurb: Former imperial temple with a palace complex and late-blooming Omuro cherries.

places.name: Ryoan-ji
